proofs.full_local_argument: Write x=(x^(1),...,x^(m)) and mu^(i)=v^(i)/n, with ||v^(i)||=||x^(i)||=1. For every feasible x, each block inner product is between -1/n and 1/n, so |mu^T x|<=m/n=1/2. Thus a valid scalar Oracle is obtained using a fresh uniform U_t independent of mu and past conditional on the chosen action: return +1 if U_t<=(1+mu^T x_t)/2 and -1 otherwise. Its conditional mean given mu, history and x_t is mu^T x_t; its values are in {-1,+1}. It can also be realized as a roundwise random cost function using the same U_t for all x; only the chosen x is evaluated. Next, Cauchy-Schwarz gives mu^(i) dot x^(i)>=-1/n for every block, with equality at x^(i)=-v^(i). These block choices jointly belong to D_n, so min_{x in D_n}mu^T x=-m/n=-1/2 for every realization of mu. Uniform circle symmetry gives E mu=0. Since x_1 is independent of mu and both are bounded, conditioning on x_1 yields E[mu^T x_1|x_1]=(E mu)^T x_1=0. Therefore E R_1=0-(-1/2)=1/2. Printed Theorem 3 claims E R_1>=n/10. At n=6 the two values are 1/2<3/5; for every larger even n the right side is still larger. Accordingly the printed all-T statement is not adopted for this construction. No step establishes a lower bound for larger T or licenses a corrected asymptotic regime.

assumptions: The first action x_1 lies in D_n and is a measurable function of public n,D_n and policy randomness independent of mu, with no prior observation or side information about mu.
Feedback at the chosen action is a scalar in {-1,+1} with conditional mean mu^T x; the action is chosen before this feedback.
statement.conclusion: E R_1=1/2. At T=1 and every even n>=6, this value is less than n sqrt(T)/10. The printed Theorem 3 inequality E R_T>=n sqrt(T)/10 for every T>=1 is therefore not adopted under this normalization.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let n=2m with m>=1 and D_n={(x^(1),...,x^(m)):x^(i) in R^2,||x^(i)||_2=1}. Draw independent uniform unit-circle vectors v^(i), and let mu^(i)=v^(i)/n. Thus mu is uniform on D_n/n. Define R_1=mu^T x_1-min_{x in D_n}mu^T x.
statement.parameter_domains: T=1; even integer n>=2. The value n sqrt(T)/10 exceeds the computed one-step regret for every even n>=6.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every even integer n>=2 and every first-action policy satisfying the information restriction, expectation over the product-uniform prior and independent policy randomness gives the stated identity. Feedback randomness can also be included without changing R_1.
